all_found.desc: [BUG] The closure row's ledger ID is the FSM run ID (mrv-...), but FINDINGS.md carry-over (carryOverLine `^- (mrvf-[A-Za-z0-9-]+) \[`) only recognizes mrvf- IDs, so the rendered Process Overrides line for a run closure is never carried over. When FINDINGS.md is re-rendered from a ledger lacking the closure row (another worktree or clone, a cleaned ledger), the committed closure audit line (actor, reason) is silently deleted.
[ADVISORY] closeRuns keys a granted closure only on run ID, not on the state/head it was closed at. A closed run later resumed and abandoned again stays hidden as closed.

[ADVISORY] closeRuns shows CloseRequestedBy for a pending row even when the run changed since the request. A resumed run displays '(close requested by X)' for a request made against an older state; unpinned by tests.

[ADVISORY] The closure snapshot is the run's last event time, and an `fsm record stopped` annotation is an event, so annotating a closed run (or one with a pending request) moves the snapshot. After a grant, `fsm record stopped` on the run reopens it as a blocker (and hides a pending request), although #179 says stopped stays an annotation that never changes a run's blocking state; the operator must request and grant again.

[ADVISORY] A grant on a pending request re-stamps the snapshot to the run's current state even when the run moved since the request. A request filed against one state can be granted and close a later state the requester never asked about; the display already treats that request as stale.

findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Closing an abandoned run with `override request|grant <run-id>` is documented in ARCHITECTURE/CLAUDE/AGENTS but not in USAGE.md's override section (the user-facing reference) nor in the override usage text. Operators facing a blocking abandoned run have no user-facing docs saying a run ID is accepted, so they still delete the run directory.

[ADVISORY] No test asserts that a repeat request on a pending closure row with an unchanged snapshot is refused and leaves the original requester intact. A regression letting a second request overwrite the first requester would go uncaught.

rejected.desc: [ADVISORY] A pending closure request has no exit if the run is later finished or its directory removed (no withdraw; Reconcile never closes it). override list --pending stays nonzero until a human grants a moot closure.
[ADVISORY] No test covers a mock run being refused a closure row, repeat/out-of-order request/grant, or a pending closure on an other-branch run. Regressions in those edges go unnoticed.

confirmed.desc: [ADVISORY] closeRuns shows CloseRequestedBy for a pending row even when the run changed since the request. A resumed run displays '(close requested by X)' for a request made against an older state; unpinned by tests.

rejected.desc: [ADVISORY] Re-closing a stale granted run closure overwrites the row in place and a direct re-grant clears the earlier requester before the requester-differs-from-grantor check. The ledger and FINDINGS.md keep only the latest cycle (the first grant's actor/reason is lost from the ledger), and the actor who requested the earlier closure can grant the new one alone — no worse than granting an open closure row with no request.

[ADVISORY] A pending request whose run resumes and is abandoned again before the grant is untested; the grant re-snapshots RunUpdated. A regression taking the snapshot from the request would let a grant close a run version the grantor never saw, with no failing test.

[ADVISORY] Only binaries with the widened carry-over regex keep a committed mrv- closure line. An older binary re-rendering FINDINGS.md from a ledger without the row drops the closure line (mixed-version setups).

fix@0.summary: carryOverLine accepts mrv- run IDs so a run closure's Process Overrides line survives a re-render from another ledger; closure rows record the run's last event (runUpdated) and closeRuns applies a grant only while it matches, with stale closures re-requestable/re-grantable; plain-text status shows closed runs, actor, reason and pending requests.

fix@1.summary: closeRuns reports CloseRequestedBy only while the run's last event matches the request's snapshot; round-1 fixes unchanged.

fix@2.summary: Closure snapshot is the run's last non-record event, so stop notes never reopen a closed run; a pending closure whose run moved is stale: re-fileable, and a grant drops the stale request.
